definition: A training technique that uses lower-precision numerical formats (like 16-bit floating point) for most computations while retaining higher precision where needed, to speed up training and reduce memory use.
details: Mixed precision training significantly reduces memory footprint and increases training throughput on modern hardware, with minimal impact on model accuracy when implemented carefully.

explainer.lead: Mixed precision training uses lower-precision formats like 16-bit floating point for most computations while retaining higher precision where needed. It matters because it cuts memory and raises throughput with minimal accuracy loss.

tiers.eli5: Use a smaller, faster number format for most of the work, and a precise one only where mistakes would hurt.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers combine low-precision math with higher-precision master weights and accumulations; a pitfall is numerical instability if sensitive operations are left in low precision.
tiers.paperLevel: Most computations use reduced-precision formats such as 16-bit floats, with higher precision retained where needed; accuracy impact is minimal when implemented carefully.

explainer.example: Training a large network with 16-bit forward and backward passes but 32-bit weight updates reduces memory footprint while keeping accuracy close to full precision.
